description: Hi everyone! I’m a Grade 7 student with a huge passion for coding, technology, and building cool projects. Programming is one of my favorite hobbies, and I am constantly picking up new languages, tools, and development concepts. Plus, with a brother who works as a software engineer, I have solid technical mentorship, best-practice tips, and high-level guidance whenever we hit tricky technical roadblocks!
summary:
During interplanetary transit beyond Low Earth Orbit, astronauts endure chronic microgravity bone loss, galactic cosmic radiation, acute solar particle events, and 14+ minute one-way communication delays to Earth. In deep space, real-time medical guidance from Mission Control is impossible.

Project Stellar Logic developed C.O.R.E. (Crew Observation & Readiness Environment), an autonomous, zero-latency aerospace health flight deck and spacesuit companion micro-interface. C.O.R.E. integrates real-time physiological telemetry (multi-lead ECG, lumbar spine DEXA bone demineralization, TEPC radiation dosimetry) with live environmental space weather streamed directly from operational NOAA/NASA GOES-18 satellites and the NASA DONKI API.

When high-energy solar storms (Class M/X flares) occur, C.O.R.E. issues automated storm-shelter evacuation orders to the crew’s radiation-shielded haven. Paired with daily behavioural check-ins computing a dynamic Crew Readiness Index (CRI %) and an asynchronous interplanetary video journal, C.O.R.E. provides deep-space crews with complete medical autonomy.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?
C.O.R.E. operates as a dual-interface mission autonomy system:
1. Habitat Flight Deck: A dark-charcoal cockpit dashboard compliant with NASA-STD-3001 human factors ergonomics. Features an interactive SVG anatomical crew wireframe displaying cardiovascular, bone density, and radiation status; a live solar vector transit trajectory; behavioral sliders calculating a 0–100% Crew Readiness Index (CRI); and a Deep Space Network communication tracker with real-world light-time delays (14m 32s OWLT).
2. Live Satellite Telemetry Bus: Streams 1-minute cadence solar X-ray flux directly from operational NOAA GOES-18 spacecraft and NASA DONKI, accompanied by a live terminal console and raw JSON packet inspector.
3. Spacesuit Wrist Companion: A wearable micro-interface with 4 glove-friendly tactile modes (Vitals, Hazard Evacuation, Quick Check-In, and an active EVA Stopwatch with suit consumables).

Tools & Technologies Used:
- Frontend: Vanilla ES Modules (zero external runtime dependencies), Tailwind CSS, Web Audio API cockpit sound synthesis.
- Backend: Vercel Edge Serverless Functions (/api/donki, /api/osdr) with Cache-Control (s-maxage=300) for edge CDN shielding and 100% offline fallback resilience.
- Satellite Integration: NOAA SWPC GOES-18 Primary XRS feed (0.1–0.8 nm) and NASA DONKI Space Weather FLR API.

Creativity & Human Factors:
Instead of static mockups, C.O.R.E. ingests live satellite data from space in real-time, features a judge simulation harness to test critical solar flares and acute tachycardia emergencies, and complies strictly with NASA display guidelines (zero pure black, low cognitive clutter, high vibration readability).
